Part A: Background and Objectives
The NPL Resolution Framework formed under the Comprehensive National Response
to the Challenges of the COVID-19 Pandemic Phase II, has brought multiple
stakeholders together to address risk and challenges of NPLs through diagnostic studies
and designing of remedial measures. The diagnostic review of NPLs highlighted the need
to standardize basic prudent requirement for credit sanctioning, monitoring and follow up
of NPLs for timely interventions to address risk of NPLs.
Therefore, these rules and regulations is being issued with the following objectives:
1. To guide Financial Service Providers (hereafter ‘FSPs’) on prudent credit risk taking
and management;
2. Provide basic prudent requirements for credit origination and sanctioning procedures;
3. To provide basic framework for monitoring of credit risk and NPL management.
Part B: Title, Extent and Commencement
1) These rules and regulations are formulated and adopted in line with Section 202 of
the FSA 2011.
2) These rules and regulations will be known as Rules and Regulations on Loan
Origination and Monitoring 2022.
3) These rules and regulations will come into force from 1st November, 2022.
4) Any relaxation on the loan origination and monitoring requirements under these rules
and regulations as part of regulatory initiative for targeted lending or relief packages
or specific policies shall be issued separately by the Authority.
5) If any issue arises in the interpretation of the provisions of these guidelines, the matter
shall be referred to the RMA, and the decision of the RMA shall be final and binding
on the stakeholders concerned.
Part C: Governance and Policies
Part C.1 Credit risk management
6) In line with Risk Management Guidelines 2019 or amendments thereof, a FSPs should
determine the level of credit risk it can bear and develop strategy that is consistent
with credit risk tolerance and its goals.
7) The FSPs shall develop credit risk culture as part of overall risk culture through
policies, communications, and training.

8) The FSP’s credit risk management shall be aligned with its overall Risk Management
Framework as per Risk Management Guidelines 2019 or amendments thereof.
9) The FSP’s credit risk management framework shall clearly specify credit risk of the
institution, composition of credit portfolio in terms of concentration and diversification
by geography, sector, and product.
10) To manage concentration risk, FSPs shall set internal credit limit for aggregate credit
risk limit for individual borrowers and related parties.
11) FSPs shall ensure that the credit policies and procedures are designed to minimize
risk of internal and external fraud in the credit granting process.
12) FSPs shall review the credit policies and procedures on a regular basis for
improvements and strengthening credit risk management.
Part C.2 Board and Management Responsibilities
13) The Board of Directors (Boards) should periodically review the credit risk strategy and
any changes and concerns should be communicated to all relevant staffs and update
the Authority accordingly.
14) The Boards of FSPs shall approve institution’s credit policies and procedures in line
with its credit risk strategy and with these rules and regulations.
15) The Boards shall approve framework for credit approval process, including but not
limited to internal structures for credit granting, monitoring, defining delegated
decision-making authorities and accountability.
16) The boards and management shall ensure effective oversight of credit risk quality in
terms of credit granting, monitoring, recovery, and provisioning.
17) The boards and management shall ensure that all staffs involved in credit risk
management are adequately trained, resourced, skilled, and experienced.
18) The boards and management should ensure there is appropriate Management
Information System to enable board and management oversight of credit risk
management in terms of credit granting, monitoring, recovery, provisioning, and
reporting. (For example, Bank should be able to identify risk of the client based on the
no. of times a loan has been declined/ rejected)
19) The boards and management shall ensure that there are frameworks and process in
place to assess the related party exposure as defined in Prudential Regulations 2017
and amendments thereof.
20) Depending on the FSP’s credit strategy, the FSP may adopt the Centralized unit
model or Hybrid model for credit operations, follow-up, collections, and recoveries.
The FSPs shall ensure there are robust control, internal audit, and follow-up review
that there are no conflicts or collusion or fraud between employees involved and the
borrowers.

Part D: Credit Sourcing and Documentation
Part D.1: Information sourcing
21) FSPs shall ensure that decisions related to credit sanctions are impartial and not
affected by conflict of interest in line with related party definitions as per Prudential
Regulations 2017 or amendments thereof.
22) FSPs shall have sufficient, accurate, and up-to-date information and data required to
assess borrower’s risk profile and credit worthiness for loan appraisal.
23) For assessing the borrower’s credit worthiness, the FSPs shall have necessary
information available and analyze as set out in annexure 1 of these rules and
regulations.
24) If FSPs have concerns on reliability and accuracy of information and data, the FSPs
shall make necessary checks and follow up with borrowers and third parties such as
employers, public offices, and databases.
25) If FSPs find that the borrower is likely to face financial difficulty in meeting contractual
loan obligations, the FSPs shall request additional information supported by
documentation demonstrating the borrower’s ability to honor their loan obligations.
Part D.2: Documentation
26) The FSPs shall maintain the complete set of loan documents and its supporting
documents in accessible form in hard copy available to competent authority for at least
the duration 10 years after closing of the loan.
27) For secured lending, the FSPs shall ensure that securities do not have double or
multiple pledging with other FSPs or missing collaterals and ensure that the mortgagor
or borrower has the legal authority to mortgage the properties as collateral or
securities against the loan.
28) However, section 27 does limit the FSPs from accepting secondary charge on the
collateral/mortgage and FSPs shall ensure there will be stringent criteria such as
lesser than standard LTV ratio and enhanced monitoring framework to ensure that
underlying collateral/mortgage stays relevant.
29) The FSP shall ensure life of collateral is more than the loan tenure. (e.g. age of the
house)
30) The FPS shall establish the legal authority to mortgage the properties, are supported
by documents or evidence in terms of secured lending.
31) The FSPs shall ensure that loan documentation process such as lien-noting, signing
of agreement and other requirements as per FSP’s credit policies and manuals, are
completed before disbursement of the loan to the borrower.
32) The FSPs shall ensure that the minimum requirements detailed in Annexure 2 are
included in the terms and conditions of the agreement. In addition, the FSPs may set
their own loan covenants covering positive, negative and financial covenants, in the
loan agreement.

33) In terms of cases where the loan sanctioned is intended for the purchase of collateral/
mortgage, the FSPs shall disburse the loan to complete the purchase of the securities
and immediately follow-up on lien-noting of the collateral and securities.
34) The FSPs shall take reasonable steps to ensure that loans disbursed to complete the
purchase of the securities are not diverted or misused by the borrower.
Part E: Credit Appraisal, Analysis and Granting
Part E.1 Appraisal
35) The FSPs shall assess and analyze the borrower’s loan application in line with
institution’s credit policies, procedures, manuals, and rules/guidelines/directives of the
RMA (including LTV and LTI requirements).
36) The Loan security shall not be a predominant criterion for loan approval and shall not
be justified for any loan approval.
37) Loan security and guarantees shall only be used as a means of securing loan recovery
in case the borrower defaults and not as primary source of repayment unless the loan
agreement stipulates that repayment of loan is based on the sale of loan security.
38) The FSPs shall take self-initiated process and procedures to assess repayment
capacity for consideration of relevant factors that could impact repayment capacity of
the borrower and the borrower’s ability to repay shall not be based on an expected
significant increase in borrower’s income unless the documents provide sufficient
evidence.
39) For joint loan application submitted by more than one borrower, FSPs shall assess
the credit worthiness of all borrowers under the joint application.
40) If a borrower is a member of a group of connected/related borrowers, FSPs shall
carry out assessment at individual level and where relevant at group based on
requirements of Prudential Regulation 2017 or amendments thereof.
41) For assessment of corporate loans, FSPs shall consider cash flow from ordinary
business activities as the primary source of loan repayment with sufficient evidence.
42) For assessment of real estate loans, FSPs shall ensure that credit worthiness
assessment of property developer and buyer shall be assessed separately, and the
sale of real estate property shall not automatically result in the property buyer
becoming credit worthy.
43) The FSPs shall ensure that there is a separate credit appraisal framework between
real estate loans and housing loans.
44) For assessment of project financing, the FSPs shall ensure that assets of the project
are pledged to financing FSP and assess the equity contribution in the project.

Part E.2: Models for creditworthiness assessment
45) The FSPs may adopt internally developed models for customer rating or credit
scoring as part of credit worthiness assessment.
46) FSPs using such models shall understand the models used, methodology, data,
assumptions, limitations, and outputs.
47) The model and its governance framework shall be based on the guidelines or SOPs
issued by the Authority.
48) The output of the model shall not automatically result in credit granting and shall
only be used a tool for creditworthiness assessment.
49) The final decision for credit granting shall be based on the overall assessment of
borrower’s credit worthiness and shall be the decision of credit granting authority.
Part E.3: Credit Decision
50) The decision to approve or decline the loan application shall be made by the
relevant credit-decision maker in accordance with policies and procedures of the
FSPs.
51) The credit decision shall clearly specify the maximum period for its validity. If
approved transaction is not executed within this period, the FSP shall re-validate the
approval.
Part E.4: Valuation of immoveable and moveable properties
52) For credit facilities secured with immoveable and moveable properties, the FSPs shall
ensure that the valuation of the security is done diligently and prudently during the
appraisal.
53) FSPs shall have internal policies and procedures for valuation of security.
Part F: Monitoring
Part F.1: Regular credit review of borrowers
54) FSPs should conduct regular credit review of borrowers for medium-large borrowers,
overdraft and working capitals. The review shall be focused but not limited to,
identifying any changes in their risk profile, financial position or creditworthiness
compared with the criteria and the assessment at the point of loan origination and
updating any internal credit rating/ scoring wherever applicable.
55) The review process and frequency should be specific and proportionate to the type
and risk profile of the borrower and the type, size, and complexity of the credit facility,
and should be specified in relevant policies and procedures. FSPs should carry out
more frequent reviews if they identify a deterioration in the credit and asset quality.
56) For medium and large borrowers, the FSPs shall periodically update relevant financial
information on the borrower and assess the new information against the
creditworthiness assessment criteria. The collection and assessment of this

information shall support the FSP in recognizing the early warning signs of declining
credit quality.
Part F.2: Monitoring of covenants and verifications
57) Where applicable, the FSPs shall monitor and follow up on security insurance in line
with loan agreement.
58) FSPs shall carry out field verification where relevant accompanied by a qualified
person, for verification of the site and retain a report in the loan file.
59) FSPs review monitor the security in terms of value, ownership, and conditions every
3 years. However, this requirements should not prelude the FSPs from carrying out
yearly review of the loans.
Part F.3: Early warning signals/ watch listing for monitoring
60) FSPs shall develop and maintain relevant quantitative and qualitative early warning
indicators (EWIs) for timely detection on increased credit risks of their credit portfolios.
61) The FSPs may adopt models for early warning signals in terms of monitoring large
borrowers and behavior scoring to identify high risk borrowers.
62) FSPs using such models shall understand the models used, methodology, data,
assumptions, limitations, and outputs.
63) The model and its governance framework shall be based on the guidelines or SOPs
issued by the Authority
64) The EWIs shall have defined trigger level set for follow up and interventions to mitigate
credit risk with defined responsibilities for the follow up actions.
65) For identified triggered EWI for borrower or a loan account, FSPs shall frequently
monitor and consider placing them on a watchlist for taking remedial measures and
mitigation actions.
66) If the follow up action include contact with borrowers, FSPs shall have regard to their
individual circumstances and may be dealt as per Rules and Regulations on Loan
Restructuring 2022 and Rules and Regulations on Foreclosure and Write-off of NPLs
or any amendments thereof.
67) The FSPs shall have heightened monitoring framework in terms of restructured loans.
Part F.4: NPL management and workout units
68) The FSPs shall establish a dedicated work out units between credit sanctioning and
legal functions.
69) The work out unit shall develop NPL case management framework.
70) The framework shall include follow-up actions with responsibilities and trigger level for
escalating the NPL cases for remedial actions within a defined time and maintain
records as per Annexure 3.

71) The escalated cases shall proceed as per Rules and Regulations on Loan
Restructuring 2022 and Rules and Regulations on Foreclosure and Write-off of NPLs
or any amendments thereof.

Annexure 1: Minimum Information and documentation to be analyses
This annex provides a set of minimum but not limited to, information, data items and evidence to
be considered and expected by the Authority from institutions and creditors when collecting
information for the purposes of creditworthiness assessment, in accordance with these guidelines.
I. General requirements:
a. Purpose of loan
b. Employment
c. Repayment source
d. Credit report from CIB
e. Collateral report from Central Registry for Secured Transaction
f. Mortgage report from Land Management System
g. History for existing borrowers
h. Evidence of tax payment ( FSPs should require borrowers to submit certified accounts
from Department of Revenue and Customs except for new business with no tax records
or micro borrowers without business licenses)
i. Evidence of collateral/ mortgage insurance (where applicable)
j. Valuation of collateral/ mortgage
k. Cost estimation in terms of construction, repair, maintenance, and purchases
l. Any other information to mitigate risk of fronting on behalf of problematic borrower
II. Real estate lending (in addition to General requirements)
a. Evidence of expertise in similar projects and assets
b. Information on any ongoing project developed by the borrower
c. Evidence of planning and permits
d. Evidence of cost estimates and timeline of project completion including any
contingencies of the development.
e. Business plan with relevant ratios.
III. Project Financing (in addition to General requirements)
a. Evidence of expertise in similar projects
b. Information on any ongoing project of the borrower
c. Evidence of planning, permits and lease documents
d. Evidence of cost estimates and timeline of project completion including any
contingencies of the development.
e. Business plan with relevant ratios.

Annexure 2: Minimum terms and conditions to be covered in the loan agreement
1. THE LOAN AMOUNT AND PURPOSE
1.1 The Loan Amount
Subject to the stipulations of the Agreement, the Lender shall make available to the
Borrower a loan of Nu. ……………. (Ngultrum) only.
1.2 Purpose of the Loan
The Loan is intended for ………………………
2. INTEREST
2.1 The interest shall be computed at ……. % per annum on simple daily product basis.
2.2 The Lender shall be entitled to revise the rate of interest on the account and in
accordance with the directives of the Board of Directors and the Royal Monetary Authority
of Bhutan and revise the amount of Monthly/Quarterly/Yearly installment accordingly for
the remaining period.
2.3 The Lender shall have the right to charge the floating rate of interest any time during the
term of the loan if the borrower has opted for floating rate.
2.4 If the Borrower fails to pay the installments and/or interest accrued on the due date and/or
in the event any of the installments or interest remaining is not paid, the Lender shall
charge, and the Borrower shall pay a late fee @ …. per annum over and above the normal
rate of interest on the………………………… (depending on the respective institution’s
computation framework which shall be approved by Board and available for RMA during
inspection)
3 TERM AND REPAYMENT
3.1 The Borrower shall repay the entire loan outstanding balance including interest
outstanding, penalty and other charges (if any) within a period of ………. Months/Years
commencing from………..
3.2 The Borrower shall repay the loan on equated monthly installment (EMI) of Nu.
……………….. (Ngultrum…………) on or before…………..day of each month as per the
repayment schedule and/or the sanction letter issued by the Lender to the Borrower until
the entire loan with accrued and unpaid interest, penalty and other charges (if any) is fully
liquidated in the record of the Lender.
3.3 The Lender shall have no legal obligation to notify the Borrower to repay the installment
on each due date. It shall be the obligation of the Borrower to ensure prompt and timely
payment of the loan to the Lender. However, this shall not limit the lender from following up
for collection of loan overdue.
3.4 Any loan repayment installment shall be first adjusted towards the accrued and unpaid
interest, the late fee/ penalty (if any) up to the date of payment and the balance amount will
be adjusted against the principal outstanding.

4 SECURITY
4.1 The Borrower shall ensure to furnish collateral/ mortgage tittle deeds and all other related
documents to the lender for creation and registration of the security interest.
4.2 The Lender shall create and register its security interest in the property through online
Central Registry for Secured Transactions (CRST)/Land Mortgage System (LMS)/with
the Registrar of Companies (ROC).
4.3 If the security is otherwise attached with freeze order from any lawful authorities or
disputed for any reason or loses commercial value due to change in its classification, the
Lender shall be entitled to immediately demand the Borrower for replacement of the
Security with another Security of equal/higher value acceptable to the Lender.
5 INSURANCE
5.1 The Borrower shall ensure that the Security is insured in favor of the Borrower and the
Lender for the insurance coverage and the value acceptable to the Lender and keep up
such insurances until the amount due under the loan is paid in full to the Lender.
5.2 If the Security is not insured at any time, the Lender shall debit the borrower’s loan account
and pay the premium. Such payment shall be deemed as part of loan disbursement subject
to applicable interest.
5.3 The Borrower shall be responsible to file the claim or initiate legal action and to do follow-
up with the Insurer in case of occurrence of risk insured and remit to the Lender the claim
received/realized from the Insurer in respect of the Security.
6 LOAN DEFAULT AND REMEDIES
In the event of any default, without prejudice to other rights and remedies available to the
Lender, the Lender shall have the right to do any or all of the following against the
Borrower/Mortgagor/Hypothecator/Guarantor, as may be permissible under applicable laws:
7.1. The right to terminate this Loan Agreement and recall the entire Loan and recover the
entire dues.
7.2. The right to suspend or freeze any withdrawal from the Loan Account of the Borrower.
7.3. The right to enforce the Security Agreement/Guarantee against the
Borrower/Mortgagor/Hypothecator/Guarantor.
7.4. The right to file a recovery suit before a court of competent jurisdiction against the
Borrower/Mortgagor/Hypothecator/Guarantor to recover the entire loan amount
outstanding, including interest(s), fees, charges and costs.
7.5. The right to seize and sell the property charged as security either by private sale or public
auction and apply the sale proceeds of such sale in or towards the liquidation of the loan
balance due to the Lender in accordance with the provisions of the Movable and
Immovable Property Act of the Kingdom of Bhutan, 1999 or any other relevant laws of the
country.
7.6. The right to claim from the Borrower the balance of any sum in the event that the sale
proceeds of the hypothecated/mortgaged Security is insufficient to discharge the loan
outstanding balance including interest(s), fees, charges and costs.

7.7. The right to claim the balance of any sum due from or against any other properties of the
Borrower not mortgaged against the Loan under this Agreement in the event that the sale
proceeds of the hypothecated/mortgaged Security is insufficient to discharge the loan
outstanding balance and the Borrower fails to pay any sum due.
7.8. The right to claim the loan outstanding balance from or against the hypothecated Security
or the estate of the Borrower or the Guarantor in the event of the death of the
Borrower/Guarantor prior to the full settlement of all dues to the Lender.
7.9. The right to publish/announce the details of the
Borrower/Mortgagor/Hypothecator/Guarantor along with the passport size photograph(s)
in the media with the leave of the court upon default of the loan(s) or for any other matter
related to the liability with the Lender and in the event that the
Borrower/Mortgagor/Hypothecator/Guarantor cannot be contacted in the address
provided in the loan application forms or this Agreement.
7.10. The right to take any other action as the Lender may deem fit for recovery of its dues and
enforcement of the securities.
7.11. Notwithstanding any indulgence shown to the Borrower in payment of installment and
interest and notwithstanding that the Lender extends the period of repayment beyond what
is stated in this Agreement, the Borrower shall remain liable for payment of all outstanding
amount together with interest at rates agreed till the final payment of all dues to the Lender.
7.12. The borrower shall not be responsible for any additional loans disbursed from the
borrower’s loan without borrower’s consent except for disbursement made as per the
terms and conditions of this agreement.
7 NOTICE
All notices, consents, demands, requests, approvals, and other communications which are
required or may be given hereunder shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly
given if delivered or mailed to the mailing address or email address specified in the loan
application forms or this Agreement.
8 LENDER’S OBLIGATION
8.1 On payment of the entire loan outstanding and any other incidental dues to the
Lender, the Lender shall issue the loan clearance letter.
8.2 If the Property is not cross collateralized against other loans, the Lender shall discharge
the lien and re-deliver the title deeds.
9 BORROWER’S INFORMATION
9.1 The Borrower hereby gives consent to the Lender to use his/her personal and credit
information to be provided to the Credit Information Bureau or any other agencies if
required by the law.
9.2 Any change in borrower’s information such as email, mobile number and contact
address should be submitted to the lender and the borrower shall update the KYC
document on time as when required by the Lender.

9.3 If the borrower has changed contact address and/or contact number without informing
the FSP and is not contactable either through the address or contact number provided
by the borrower in the loan document for a period of 60 days from the day of default, the
borrower shall be classified as untraceable, and the same status shall be submitted to
Credit Information Bureau.
10 GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION FOR DISPUTE SETTLEMENT
This Agreement shall be governed by the relevant laws of the Kingdom of Bhutan. Any dispute
arising out of and/or in connection with this Agreement shall be submitted to the court of
competent jurisdiction in Bhutan for adjudication.

1. PRELIMINARY
It is crucial that the Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan (hereafter referred to as the Authority)
continues to take timely and appropriate action when the Financial Service Providers (FSPs)
fail to comply with the regulatory requirements that are imposed on them in order to ensure the
safety, soundness, and stability in the financial system in the overall national interest.
In order to ensure transparency and impartiality of the Authority’s decisions, these amended
rules and regulations are issued in pursuant to Section 167 of the Financial Services Act of
Bhutan 2011 (referred to as FSAB 2011 herafter) to provide overall principles and
methodologies to determine and impose administrative penalties on the FSPs for violating any
provision of rules, regulations, guidelines, directives, circulars, notifications, observations, and
timelines set out and issued by the Authority from time to time in line with the Acts (the Royal
Monetary Act of Bhutan 2010 and Financial Services Act of Bhutan 2011, whichever is
applicable).
2. TITLE, COMMENCEMENT, AND APPLICATION
This framework shall:
a) Be called the Penalty Rules and Regulations 2022;
b) Come into force on 1st July 2022; and
c) Shall apply to all:
i. Financial institutions licensed by the Authority under the Acts;
ii. Financial services providers licensed/registered with the Authority under the
provisions of the Acts; and
iii. Any person who is governed by these rules and regulations framed and enforced by
the Authority.
3. REPEAL AND SAVING
Upon adoption of the amended rules and regulations by the Board (RMA):
a) The Penalty Rules and Regulations 2019 shall stand repealed;
b) Supersede any circular, guideline, references or notifications that are inconsistent with
these rules and regulations; and
c) All actions taken by the Authority under the Penalty Rules and Regulations 2019 shall stand
until appropriate remedies or rectifications are carried out by the FSPs.
3

4. AUTHORITY
In pursuant to the power vested under Section 167 of FSAB 2011, the Authority hereby issues
the amended rules and regulations to impose appropriate penalty/ies on the FSPs for violations
specified under Section 9 of these rules and regulations.
5. INTERPRETATION
The Authority shall interpret any provision of the rules and regulations and its interpretation
shall be final and binding on the FSPs.
6. REVIEW AND AMENDMENT
The Authority shall review the rules and regulations including the penalty matrix from time to
time and make amendments where necessary.
7. DEFINITIONS
a) Unless otherwise specified, the terms and terminology used in the rules and regulations
shall bear the same meaning defined in the Acts;
b) The term “Authority” means Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan as defined in the RMA
Act 2010;
c) The term “Acts” means Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan Act of Bhutan 2010 and
Financial Services Act of Bhutan 2011; and
d) The term “Board” means the Board of the Authority established under Section 28 of the
RMA Act of Bhutan 2010.
8. OBJECTIVES
The objective of these rules and regulations is to provide broad provisions for assessing and
imposing monetary penalties, mainly to:
a) Enhance the integrity and credibility of the FSPs by ensuring that violations specified under
Section 9 of the rules and regulations are detected early, strictly monitored and
contraventions, if any, are accordingly penalized;
b) Provide guidance for the assessment of the nature of administrative and quantum of
administrative penalties and corrective actions to be directed by the Authority; and
4

c) Deter the FSPs for violating any provisions of the of rules, regulations, guidelines,
directives, circulars, notifications, observations, and timelines issued by the Authority in
line with the Acts.
9. VIOLATIONS
The Authority shall consider violations eligible for monetary penalties including, but not
limited to, the following:
a) Violation of the Acts, rules, regulations, guidelines, directives, circulars, and notifications
issued by the Authority and specified in Appendix B;
b) Non-compliance with the observations/findings/corrective actions within the timelines
prescribed by the Authority;
c) Contraventions that are tantamount to offence and not covered by these rules and
regulations; and
d) Notwithstanding the above provisions, offences that are clearly stipulated with a penalty in
the Acts shall be dealt with as per the provisions of the respective Acts.
10. FACTORS
The following factors shall be considered for determining the quantum of penalties as stipulated
in the Matrix (refer to Appendix A)
a) Severity;
b) Intent;
c) History and frequency of violations; and
d) Effectiveness of internal control and compliance management systems.
11. PROCEDURES AND TIMELINES
The Authority shall administer the following procedures sequentially and the specified timeline
to identify and impose a monetary penalty on FSPs:
a) Identification and Assessment of Violations:
i. The departments concerned of the Authority shall identify the violation/s through its
oversight, monitoring and other supervisory and surveillance mechanism;
5

ii. The departments concerned shall document its recommendation/s and include the
completed Penalty Matrix (refer to Appendix A) along with the supporting documents
to determine the level of action required;
iii. The departments concerned shall refer to the Guide (Appendix A) to complete the
Penalty Matrix to ensure that the penalty is imposed consistently and equitably; and
iv. The findings and recommendations along with the necessary supporting document shall
be submitted to the Legal Services Department for consultation and imposition of
penalties.
b) Written Notice
i. If a decision is made by the department concerned to impose penalty on the FSP,
the decision shall be communicated through a written notice (14-day notice as per
Section 157 of FSA 2011) to the FSP by the Legal Services Department;
ii. The written notice shall be served within seven (7) working days from the date of
identification of violation(s) through off-site surveillance and within thirty (30)
days from the date of completion of the examination for violation(s) identified
through on-site supervision; and
iii. The written notice issued to FSP concerned, among other things, shall include the
following:
a. Seek explanation and or additional documentary evidence from the FSP
concerned within fourteen (14) days from the date of issuance;
b. Inform the intent of the Authority to impose appropriate penalties; and
c. Provide an opportunity to FSPs for submitting additional documentary
evidence to the Authority for review and consideration of the penalties as
per the timelines set out.
c) Penalty or No-Penalty Order
i. Based on the receipt/non-receipt of explanations from the FSPs within the fourteen
(14) day notice, the Legal Services Department shall decide the next course of
action;
ii. If satisfactory explanations not to impose penalties are furnished by the FSP, the
the Legal Services Department may issue No-Penalty Order or reprimand letter in
lieu of penalty to the FSP;
6

iii. If the department concerned is not satisfied with the explanations furnished by the
FSP, a Penalty Order with the amount of penalty and the penalty matrix prepared
for the purpose shall be issued to the FSP;
iv. The Penalty Order may include corrective actions with specific timelines for
compliance/rectification; and
v. The above procedure to issue a Penalty or No-Penalty Order shall be completed
within seven (7) working days from the receipt of explanations/reasons to that
effect.
d) Payment of Penalty:
i. The penalty imposed on an FSP shall be payable to the Authority within a period of
thirty (30) days from the date of issue of Penalty Order;
ii. In the case of FSPs that maintain a current account with the Authority, the
Department of Banking shall debit the account of the FSP concerned upon receipt
of an order of the same from the Legal Services Department;
iii. The Department of Banking shall maintain a specific account for this purpose; and
iv. In case of failure in payment of penalty amount, the Authority shall initiate
appropriate action to impose an additional penalty not exceedingly twice the amount
of the penalty as per Section 168 of FSAB 2011.
e) Appeal
i. In pursuant to Section 162 of FSAB 2011, the FSP concerned issued with Penalty
Order may appeal to the Authority’s Board in writing within fourteen (14) days of
the issue of order;
ii. The appeal shall be routed through the Board of FSP;
iii. The Board of Authority shall affirm, reverse, modify or maintain status quo the
decision and state its legal and factual grounds; and
iv. The decision made by the Board may be appealed within twenty one (21) days to a
court of jurisdiction if the FSPs so wish.
f) Public Disclosure
i. The Authority shall disclose the name of the FSP on the Authority’s websites or
any media channels deemed appropriate including the amount and contravention
after a Penalty Order is issued to the FSP.
7

PENALTY CALCULATION METHODOLOGY
Guide for using the Penalty Matrix for FSPs
A. Number of matrices: One matrix shall be completed per FSP for all or one violation.
When there are several violations included in one matrix, the highest severity level
applicable for any of them will be recorded for each factor in the matrix.
B. The following definitions apply when using the matrix:
1. Violations include violations of Acts, rules, regulations, guidelines, directives,
circulars, and notifications issued by the Authority from time to time.
C. Factors:
1. Concealment: This factor pertains to the concealment of a violation or reckless
unsafe or unsound practice from the Authority, FSP’s board of directors,
internal and external auditors, or other regulatory agencies.
2. Continuation after notification: “notification “in this factor includes notice
issued by the Authority, other regulatory agencies, internal and external
auditors, containing information, but not limited to the existence of a violation,
unsafe practice, etc.
3. Repetition of violation from previous years: “Similar violation” may refer to
previous violations of the same statute or regulation, for example, a previous
Capital Adequacy Ratio requirement violation and a current Capital Adequacy
Ratio requirement violation. Violations that were identified in earlier
examinations should be considered in applying this factor, even if they have
been corrected. If a previously corrected violation or deficiency resurfaces later,
this may indicate a weakness in the bank’s compliance management system or
internal controls.
4. Duration and frequency of violations before notification: This factor refers to
the time period during which the violation(s) at issue continued and the number
of the violations at issue. “Notification” in this factor means the same as that
under “Continuation after notification.” Under severity level 2, “practice”
includes if the conduct of violations is prescribed in the FSP's internal policies
and procedures.
5. Financial gain or loss to the FSP as a result of violation: Includes any direct or
indirect monetary gain or loss to the FSP.
6. Impact or harm other than the financial loss to the FSP: Impact or harm other
than financial loss can be any possible negative impact or harm such as
10

increased reputation risk, operational risk, or compliance risk to the FSP. It can
also include harm to consumers or to the public resulting from the violations.
7. Effectiveness of Internal Controls and Compliance Management systems: This
factor is to evaluate whether and how a bank’s internal controls or compliance
programs, or lack thereof, contributed to the violation or deficiency in question.
Internal control systems or compliance programs that are so lacking as to permit
the violation or deficiency to occur and remain undetected should be accorded
the most severe score. Internal control systems or compliance programs that
identified the violation or deficiency, which allowed the bank to initiate timely
corrective measures, may receive a lower score.

Editions of Corporate Governance Rules and Regulations
